title: Meaningful associations in the adolescent brain cognitive development study

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Meaningful associations in the adolescent brain cognitive development study》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-5】Here, we describe the ABCD Study aims and design, as well as issues surrounding estimation of meaningful associations using its data, including population inferences, hypothesis testing, power and precision, control of covariates, interpretation of associations, and recommended best practices for reproducible research, analytical procedures and reporting of results.

evidence.text: Here, we describe the ABCD Study aims and design, as well as issues surrounding estimation of meaningful associations using its data, including population inferences, hypothesis testing, power and precision, control of covariates, interpretation of associations, and recommended best practices for reproducible research, analytical procedures and reporting of results.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Meaningful associations in the adolescent brain cognitive development study》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】The Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study is the largest single-cohort prospective longitudinal study of neurodevelopment and children's health in the United States.

【Abstract · abstract-1-2】A cohort of n = 11,880 children aged 9-10 years (and their parents/guardians) were recruited across 22 sites and are being followed with in-person visits on an annual basis for at least 10 years.

evidence.text: The Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study is the largest single-cohort prospective longitudinal study of neurodevelopment and children's health in the United States.
A cohort of n = 11,880 children aged 9-10 years (and their parents/guardians) were recruited across 22 sites and are being followed with in-person visits on an annual basis for at least 10 years.
